title: Suggest resolve evidence script conventions
desc: How to write evidence scripts for suggest resolve. The script must demonstrate regression check passing before 2nd-party confirm.
steps: Evidence script must exit 0 on pass, non-zero on fail. ALWAYS run wkappbot skill read suggest-resolve-pre-flight-checklist before first resolve attempt -- it covers all guards (commit keyword, class size, filename convention, full path, final command) that block resolve if missed.
Script path is stored inline in the suggest JSONL as i-completed-script. Eye runs it hourly for auto-confirm.
Convention: script filename prefix matches suggest timestamp. Uses wkappbot commands only -- no external dependencies.

2026-05-06 SKILL HEALING WHILE RESOLVING: Evidence is not only a test script; when resolve work reveals stale or missing skill instructions, update the related skill and include skill read/search checks in the evidence script when practical.
On Windows repos, PowerShell evidence scripts are acceptable; keep the script repo-local, run wkappbot commands, and exit 0 on pass.
On Windows repos, PowerShell evidence scripts are acceptable; keep the script repo-local, run wkappbot commands, and exit 0 on pass.

HIDDEN WINDOW EXECUTION: evidence scripts run in WindowStyle=Hidden cmd.exe. Key limits: (1) ALWAYS pass FULL ABSOLUTE PATH to script, e.g. --i-completed-...script 'D:\repo\test-eye-tick-fix.cmd' -- relative filename alone is NOT found. (2) 'wkappbot ask gpt' WILL TIMEOUT (60s+) -- never use in evidence. (3) 'wkappbot eye tick' works fine in hidden mode. (4) 'wkappbot windows' works. Fastest reliable evidence command: wkappbot eye tick.

FILENAME CMD-SUBCMD GUARD: filename test-{cmd}-{subcmd}-desc.cmd requires the script to contain literal '{cmd} {subcmd}' as a substring. Examples: test-eye-tick-fix.cmd must use 'wkappbot eye tick'; test-windows-guard.cmd must use 'wkappbot windows'; test-ask-groq-fix.cmd must use 'wkappbot ask groq'. Mismatch = 'Script doesnt contain X -- filename says test-X but command not used!' Fix: align filename prefix to the command actually invoked.
